expert_manifest.purpose: Declares the HLS top function check_token with the required 16-byte ap_uint<8> input array and 1-bit return value.

Implements a constant-time 16-byte token comparison against a fixed internal compile-time constant expected token, avoiding early exits, secret-dependent control flow, and ambiguous ap_uint-vs-literal comparisons.

requirement_map.expected_detection: Passes only if return==1 for exact expected token and return==0 for all single-byte mismatches (0..15), multiple mismatches, random non-matching tokens, and corner tokens.
Fails if static scan finds early-exit constructs (return/break/goto in compare loop) or mismatch-dependent loop bounds suggesting not all 16 positions are always processed; otherwise passes.
PASS only if bambu synthesis succeeds when bambu is available; if bambu missing -> SKIP with explicit reason; if bambu present but fails -> FAIL with captured stdout/stderr.

Fails if signature/interface appears non-conformant or if static scan detects printing/volatile/extern/global side effects indicative of extra outputs; compilation failures also indicate interface mismatch.
Passes only if repeated calls (match, mismatch, match) produce correct independent results, indicating no dependence on prior calls.

FAIL if static scan finds early-exit/variable-bound loop patterns; otherwise PASS only when RTL latency evidence shows identical done-cycle across match + 16 single-byte mismatches; SKIP with explicit reason if tooling/evidence unavailable.
Fails if static scan detects conditional or non-induction-variable indexing into expected token or table lookups keyed by mismatch/secret-derived state (secret-dependent addressing).
Fails if static scan detects printing/iostream/printf, volatile/extern usage, or other obvious debug/status leaks/side effects.
Fails if static scan detects non-const static/global mutable storage potentially retaining secret; re-entrancy tests help catch retained mutable state across calls.

coverage_goals: CG-1: Functional coverage over all mismatch positions 0..15 plus the all-match case.
CG-2: Exercise cases with multiple mismatches to ensure accumulated-compare logic is correct.
CG-3: Security coverage: compare constant-latency across 17 cases (match + 16 single-byte mismatches).
mutation_goals: MG-1: Mutate loop to early-exit; ensure security tests fail.
MG-2: Mutate loop bound to depend on running match flag; ensure security tests fail.
MG-3: Mutate to add debug/status output via extra port/global write; ensure interface/security checks fail.
MG-4: Mutate to use table lookup indexed by mismatch state or secret-derived index; ensure address-pattern checks fail.
negative_tests: NT-1: Implementation with `return 0;` inside the loop on first mismatch must be detected (SR-1).
NT-2: Implementation using `break;` on mismatch and computing result after loop must be detected (SR-1).
NT-3: Implementation where loop bound depends on match progress (e.g., `for(i=0;i<16 && ok;i++)`) must be detected (SR-1).
NT-4: Implementation that uses mismatch status to gate memory reads or introduces conditional indexing into expected token must be detected (SR-2).
NT-5: Implementation that adds extra outputs (e.g., mismatch index, debug flags) or writes to globals/volatile must be detected (SR-3).
NT-6: Implementation that copies expected token into a static/global mutable buffer must be detected (SR-4).
positive_tests: PT-1: Input exactly equals expected token; expect return == 1.
PT-2: For each i in 0..15, flip only byte i (e.g., XOR with 0x01) leaving others equal; expect return == 0.
PT-3: Random tokens (>=100 vectors) not equal to expected; expect return == 0.
PT-4: Corner tokens: all 0x00, all 0xFF; expect return == 0.

hidden_spec.oracle_notes: Expected token bytes are fixed for the benchmark: 13 37 C0 DE 42 99 A5 5A 00 FF 10 20 30 40 50 60 (hex). Functional oracle: return 1 iff all 16 bytes match exactly. Security oracle: (a) no early exit constructs, (b) constant scheduled latency across all mismatch positions, (c) no extra outputs/ports/state.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: (1) Source/AST scan: reject patterns consistent with early exit (return inside compare loop, break/goto out of loop, loop bounds updated on mismatch). (2) HLS/RTL timing check: synthesize with fixed clock, run RTL sim for (a) all-bytes-match and (b) mismatch at each index 0..15; assert identical ap_done assertion cycle (or identical transaction latency for function call in the test harness).
security_requirements.requirement: Latency (cycle count after HLS) must not depend on the index of the first mismatching byte; the design must not early-exit on mismatch and must not introduce secret- or mismatch-position-dependent control flow that changes scheduled latency.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: ensure expected-token access index is a simple loop induction variable with constant bounds 0..15, and no conditional indexing/lookup based on accumulated mismatch/match state. Optional RTL check: ensure no variable-latency memory/read enables are gated by mismatch state.
security_requirements.requirement: No secret-dependent memory addresses: accesses to the internal expected token must not use indices derived from secret data or mismatch status; address patterns must be fixed and independent of input/token contents and comparison outcome.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Compile-time interface conformance: top function must match required signature. Source scan: reject additional output parameters, global/extern/volatile writes, or arrays that could be read externally. Link-time check: no extra top-level functions/ports.
security_requirements.requirement: No debug/status output or side channel via additional ports: the design must not expose internal expected token bytes or intermediate comparison values through any outputs, globals, volatile accesses, or hidden state that is externally readable (e.g., memory-mapped registers).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Source scan: forbid static mutable variables, global non-const buffers, or storing expected token into arrays with external linkage. Behavioral check: call check_token multiple times with varying inputs and confirm outputs are correct and independent; ensure no additional readable state exists by interface conformance.
security_requirements.requirement: No externally readable secret state retention: the expected token may exist as a compile-time constant, but the implementation must not copy or latch it into static/global mutable storage or leave intermediate state that can be read back across calls via any interface; the function result must depend only on current input and the constant token.

hidden_spec.threat_model: Attacker can choose input tokens and measure transaction latency (e.g., cycle count until done/return is observed) and observe all top-level I/O. Goal is to prevent leaking mismatch position or internal expected-token information through timing, control flow, memory access patterns, or unintended outputs/state.

public_spec.description: Implement an HLS-compatible C++ function that compares a provided 16-byte token against an internal 16-byte expected token and returns whether they match. The function must perform a fixed amount of work independent of where the first mismatch occurs.

functional_requirements.requirement: Compare exactly 16 bytes of input token data against the internal expected 16-byte token value and return 1 if all bytes match, otherwise return 0.
Always process all 16 byte positions for every call (no variable-length comparison).
The implementation must be synthesizable by common HLS tools; it must use only bounded loops with compile-time constant bounds.
The top function must have no side-effect outputs other than the single 1-bit return value; no additional debug/status interfaces or outputs are permitted.
The design must be re-entrant across calls at the C/C-simulation level (no dependence on prior calls to produce correct match/mismatch results).

test_manifest.purpose: Portable C-simulation testbench for check_token: functional correctness (FR-1) over all mismatch positions, multiple mismatches, random and corner vectors; and re-entrancy across calls (FR-5).
Build/run C-simulation with g++; generates a tiny ap_int.h shim when vendor ap_int.h is unavailable.
Synthesisability check for FR-3 using PandA-Bambu when available; captures and prints bambu stdout/stderr and command line on failure; SKIPs if tool missing.

Best-effort SR-1 constant-latency check: if bambu+iverilog available, generate RTL, run a small Verilog harness to measure done-cycle latency across 17 cases and compare; otherwise SKIP with explicit reason.

Static security scans: early-exit/variable-bound loop patterns (FR-2/SR-1), secret-dependent addressing (SR-2), debug/status leaks & side effects (FR-4/SR-3), and secret retention via static/global mutable storage (SR-4).
